description: We are a motivated and creative team interested in psychology, space exploration, and human well-being. Our idea is to develop an innovative tool for monitoring astronauts' psychological states during space missions. The system aims to track emotional changes, stress levels, and signs of psychological fatigue, helping identify potential difficulties early. We welcome teammates interested in psychology, programming, data analysis, design, and technology.
summary:
Our project focuses on developing smart software for monitoring astronauts' health during space missions. The system uses smartwatches and special sensors to track important physical and psychological indicators, such as heart rate, sleep quality, stress levels, physical activity, and emotional state.

The software analyzes the collected data and helps identify signs of stress, fatigue, sleep disturbances, and possible psychological difficulties. It provides astronauts and mission specialists with information about their well-being, allowing them to respond to potential problems in time.

Our goal is to support not only astronauts' physical health but also their mental well-being. This is especially important because space missions involve isolation, high stress, limited communication, and unusual living conditions. By monitoring both physical and psychological health, our project can help improve astronauts' safety, performance, and quality of life during long-term space missions.
details:
Our project involves developing a smart device and software system for monitoring astronauts' physical and psychological health during space missions.

The device will use special sensors to collect information about heart rate, sleep quality, physical activity, stress levels, and other important health indicators. The software will analyze this information, track changes, and help identify possible signs of fatigue, emotional stress, and psychological overload. If unusual changes are detected, the system will be able to send alerts to astronauts and mission specialists.

The main advantage of our project is that it combines physical and psychological health monitoring in one device. It will not only track the body's condition but also help pay attention to astronauts' emotional well-being.

The expected impact of the project is to improve astronauts' safety and living conditions in space, identify potential health problems early, and provide necessary support during long-term missions.

Our concept is based on the use of a smartwatch, biometric sensors, data analysis software, and an alert system. These technologies will work together to collect and analyze health information in real time.

The creativity of our project lies in its focus on both physical health and psychological well-being. We want to develop a technology that helps understand astronauts' needs and supports them even in conditions of isolation in space.

During the development of our project, we considered the specific challenges of the space environment, including isolation, stress, sleep disturbances, limited communication, device autonomy, measurement accuracy, comfort, and personal data protection.
